blocks.text: Episode 107 opens with the Sakhi of Babur and explicitly announces a retrospective turn away from Taru Singh's immediate scene toward the older cause of Guru-suffering. The page frames this as the beginning of an explanatory history rather than a break in devotional seriousness.

Using the comparison of an incautious boon, the poet says Guru Nanak's utterance toward Babur later required endurance and suffering for the sake of the Sikhs. Readers are asked to listen closely because the new episode explains how a spoken blessing can reverberate through later generations.

From there the narration starts laying out the political stage around Talvandi Rai Bhoi, Daulat Khan Lodhi, and the conditions that will draw Babur into the story. The page therefore functions as both a fresh episode opening and a deliberate return to early historical causation.
